title: Moving Averages and Borwein Integrals Visualization
full_prompt: Write a complete Manim script to visualize the concept of moving averages and convolutions leading to the Borwein integral phenomenon. The scene should contain two coordinate systems (axes): an upper one for the original function and a lower one for the resulting convolution. First, plot a rectangular step function f_1(x) (which is 1.0 on [-0.5, 0.5] and 0.0 elsewhere) on the upper axes. Animate a glowing dot tracing this step function. Next, transition the layout by shrinking the upper axes and f_1(x) label to the top-right, and introducing a second set of axes at the bottom. Then, iteratively compute and display the convolutions f_{n+1}(x) on the lower axes. For each iteration, visualize a sliding window (representing the moving average) moving across the upper graph to generate the lower graph. Highlight the flat plateau at the top of each convolution graph with a yellow line, a brace, and a label indicating its width (which decreases as 1 - sum_{k=3}^{2n+1} 1/k). Also, display the value of f_{n+1}(0) on the screen, showing that it remains exactly 1.0 for the first several iterations, but eventually drops slightly below 1.0 (e.g., to 0.9999999999852937...) when the plateau width becomes negative.

visual_techniques: Dual coordinate systems (upper and lower axes)

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect coordinate mapping between upper and lower axes
common_failure_modes.note: The sliding window must align precisely with the upper axes while drawing the resulting convolution on the lower axes.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Failure to compute convolutions numerically in real-time
common_failure_modes.note: Pre-computing or using highly optimized numpy arrays for the convolution graphs is necessary to avoid extremely slow rendering times.
The plateau width formula must correctly evaluate to 0 or negative, and the brace must handle zero-width cases gracefully without throwing errors.
